facts.fact: The Tony Blair Institute states that King Faisal Hospital Rwanda, a Kigali referral hospital, replaced multiple and sometimes paper-based systems used before 2024 with an Integrated Health Management Information System joining administrative and clinical areas (imaging and laboratory among them) so that each patient has a single record; one hospital only, and no date is given beyond the document's publication.

systems.country_label: Integrated Health Management Information System (King Faisal Hospital Rwanda)
systems.owner: King Faisal Hospital Rwanda, with the ministries of health and ICT; Tony Blair Institute advised on design

systems.tiers: to be rolled out to all hospitals and health centres; no deployment figure stated
national hub integrating data from hospitals, health centres, supply chains and workforce management; launched April 2025

note: The document also says that before the NHIC, facility managers spent two or three days each month-end manually recording data to send to the Ministry of Health, and that records can now flow directly into the NHIC; it names no reporting system and does not say where that data was keyed, so no hmis fact is taken. For e-Buzima it states an intention to roll out, not a deployment.
